title: Minimax Risk for Long-Term Effects on the Treated with a Weak Outcome Bridge
banked_reason: The promised full structural Gaussian experiment, including every realizable nuisance direction and reverse lifting, is left open; the proved included four-coordinate chart is not a substitute for that deliverable.
gap_reasons: The promised full structural Gaussian experiment, including every realizable nuisance direction and reverse lifting, is left open; the proved included four-coordinate chart is not a substitute for that deliverable.

The projected paper score is limited by the specially coupled law class, the absence of a full limit-experiment characterization, and the lack of evidence connecting the binary frontier to the continuous-spline empirical consumer.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived matched weak-bridge risk and honest-length rates for a strict finite binary structural subclass, with adaptive ridge/projection procedures and full-likelihood lower bounds. Two proposed reverse-lifting arguments for the full arbitrary-base critical Gaussian experiment failed because pointwise latent interiority does not provide uniform weak-scale reconstruction bounds. The included critical chart is retained, while the full structural score image and reverse lifting remain open; the fresh math review passed and the general review graded the delivered package subfield.
tldr: In a strict finite-support specialization of the Chen--Xie and Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang outcome-bridge branch, augmented by observed-cell positivity, a uniform latent-propensity margin, bounded bridge coordinates, and \(\delta_n\)-indexed weak/loading bands, the exact nonnegative-kernel source image and the complete two-source product likelihood yield, for all sufficiently large \(n\) and \(0<\delta_n\le\delta_\star\), the matched ALTTE mean-squared-error frontier \(n^{-1}+\min\{\delta_n,(n\delta_n)^{-1}\}\) and honest expected-length frontier \(n^{-1/2}+\min\{\delta_n^{1/2},(n\delta_n)^{-1/2}\}\); the upper bounds hold on the full stated range \(0<\delta_n\le\delta_0\). A ridge estimator and a source-compatible projection interval attain these orders without knowing \(\delta_n\). The three regimes are separated by the regular-floor crossover \(\delta_n\asymp n^{-1}\) and the weak-identification elbow \(\delta_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\). An included, structurally realizable linked-denominator chart proves complete-product-likelihood LAN only at the latter elbow; the full structural Gaussian experiment remains open. Neither the subclass upper nor lower bounds transfer to the unrestricted published models, and the binary result does not validate the continuous-spline Job Corps and SIPP application.
gap: Fixed-law efficiency theory does not determine risk or honest interval length when bridge rank and target loading vanish together. Generic binary projection inference does not supply a \(\delta_n\)-dependent length frontier, and substituting an unrestricted bridge-moment outer model for the strict binary subclass omits observable restrictions imposed by its two common-latent source equations.
fill: The project pairs a deterministic modulus and \(\delta_n\)-blind procedures over the compact augmented closure with source-compatible product-likelihood lower alternatives, then uses finite latent Jacobian elimination and reverse lifting to characterize every nuisance direction in the explicitly based critical Gaussian experiment.
